encounters.weakness: The player's Neural Pulse Dampener can disrupt its signal lock. If used during a power surge, it triggers a 30% chance of disabling the drone for 5 seconds. The drone relies on AI-assisted targeting, making it vulnerable during pulse disruptions.

The Enforcer has a secondary cybernetic eye that relies on external signal input. If the player uses the Decay Chip to hack its external node, the eye goes blind for 7 seconds. This reveals its blind spots — allowing the player to dodge attacks and land critical hits. Using the Decay Chip here is mandatory to progress.

The Overlord is vulnerable when exposed to the *Decay Chip (Type-9)*, which it initially rejected during earlier phases. However, the player must use the *Coolant Surge Canister* to destabilize its thermal core first. Once the core is overheated, the Decay Chip can be inserted into its primary data node to trigger a cascade failure. The Decay Chip must be used *within 3 seconds* of the core overheating, or the boss regains full control.

Neural Pulse Blade (pulse emission activates weak point in its core data stream). When blade is drawn and pulsed, it causes a feedback surge in the Wraith's neural field, reducing damage taken by 30% and creating a 3-second stun window for melee attacks. Wraith attacks by projecting false shadows that mimic the player's movements (psychic mimicry).

Neural Pulse Shard (when used directly during combat, the shard disrupts the Siren's internal feedback loop. A single use causes a 4-second EMP stutter, during which the Siren takes 50% more damage and is vulnerable to melee attacks. The Siren's cybernetic limbs can be damaged by pulse bursts if the blade is close to the joints.)

Flesh Circuit Core (must be equipped during the final phase to trigger 'Bio-Override'). When the player equips the Flesh Circuit Core and attacks the core's central node, it triggers a feedback loop that disables the Hollow Core's network replication and causes a 10-second vulnerability window. During this, all damage is amplified by 50%, and it is vulnerable to the player's Neural Pulse Blade. If not used in time, the Hollow Core reactivates with a 'data reintegration' phase that summons two minor enemies (Data Wraith and Rust Siren clones) and regenerates 200 health in 2 seconds. This phase is immune to all attacks until the Flesh Circuit Core is used again.
Pulse Echo Mod (player weapon) - causes dissonance in its synthetic core, triggering a 15% damage boost and 20% stun chance when fired at 100% charge.

Circuit Echo Core (pickup from previous encounter) - when used in conjunction with a direct hit, causes the drone to short-circuit and explode in 3 seconds, dealing 120% damage and leaving a temporary EMP field.

Neural Resonance Shard (acquired in Encounter 1) - when used, the Weaver's core destabilizes. It emits a scream, and its health is reduced by 35%. Additionally, it enters 'Fragile Resonance' state, making it vulnerable to player's Circuit Pistol for 10 seconds.
Chrono-Scythe (slows enemy movement by 20% for 3 seconds during time-drip attack)
Fractured Chrono-Resonator (when activated, slows the enemy's regeneration cycle and forces it to repeat its attack loop — freezing it in a time-loop for 2 seconds).
Temporal Anchor (if used during the boss's rewind phase, it halts its time-loop for 5 seconds, allowing the player to deal damage before it resets).

The player's Neural Alchemist's Flask emits a low-frequency pulse that disrupts the Drift's bio-circuitry. When the flask is activated, it causes the Drift to stutter and emit erratic spikes. This triggers a feedback loop where it momentarily drops to 30% health for 2 seconds. The Flask must be used immediately after the first hit to activate this effect (cooldown: 4 seconds).

The Mnemonist absorbs and mimics the player's actions. If the player uses the **Ferro-Flame Residue** (from prior encounter) within 3 seconds of the first hit, the Mnemonist begins to hallucinate and misfires its attacks. For 3 seconds, it attacks only at 50% damage, and its movement is slowed by 30%. This only works once per encounter.

The Vault Mind is a sentient AI that replicates the player's actions. It is vulnerable to the **Neural Soot Core**, which was obtained in the second encounter. When the player uses the Soot Core *after* the first hit, the Vault Mind enters a recursive loop where it attempts to copy the player's actions in reverse — causing it to freeze for 5 seconds, and then drop to 60% health. This only works if the Soot Core is applied *within 3 seconds of the first attack*. After this, the Core depletes and cannot be reused. The player must use it at the exact moment of first contact to succeed. Failure results in a full regeneration of the AI (hard difficulty).

The player's Neural Pulse Rifle can disrupt its bio-mechanical nervous system. The rifle's pulse frequency (12.7 Hz) matches the Hound's core oscillation frequency, causing a 40% damage boost when fired at close range. Use the rifle's pulse setting to stagger and weaken the Hound before it attacks with its serrated claws and acid spray.

The Iron Sprocket's primary power source is a stolen data-core. If the player uses the Fiber-Link Fragment to emit a targeted signal (specifically, 7.3 Hz), it causes a feedback surge in the Sprocket's core, reducing its health by 35% per hit. The Fragment must be active and used during the first 10 seconds of the encounter to initiate the chain reaction. After that, the Sprocket gains a temporary shield that absorbs 50% of incoming damage.

The boss is built from the remnants of abandoned data-sentinels. Its core is fused with a corrupted AI fragment — the one that once powered the *Fiber-Link Fragment* during the first encounter. If the player uses the Neural Static Shard to activate a full-pattern sync (by pressing the 'Sync' button in the NP-Rifle while the shard is in the weapon), the boss's entire network malfunctions, causing it to freeze for 10 seconds and become vulnerable to all attacks. This sync only works if the player had collected the Fiber-Link Fragment *during* the first encounter (i.e., used it to survive or activate the environment).
Storm Blade (lightning cuts through fog, revealing hidden paths and disrupting fog generation). Fog burns when hit by the blade's current, causing it to dissipate in 2 seconds.
Lightning Puddles (when stepped on, puddles explode and release a burst of static energy that disrupts Pia's glitch rhythm and freezes her for 3 seconds).
Glowing Storm Seed (if used in a targeted storm burst, causes a full explosion that shatters the entity's core. It cannot take damage from lightning or fog — only from the seed's pure storm energy).

The Geomantic Tectonic Drill's low-frequency hum disrupts its root network. When the player uses the drill to emit a soft harmonic pulse (a passive geomantic resonance), it causes the wraith to tremble and lose stability, taking 20% damage per second for 5 seconds.

The player must use the Resonance Shard to activate a 'vibration dampener' effect. When the shard is active, the golem's sand structure becomes brittle. It takes 35% damage per second for 8 seconds when hit by a geomantic gravity pull (player can use gravity shift to pull sand into spikes).

The Eclipse Sentinel is weakened when the player uses the **Gravity Anchor Core** while in proximity to a Resonance Shard. When both are active simultaneously, the Sentinel's root network collapses, and it takes 50% damage per second for 10 seconds. This creates a temporary vulnerability window. Without both, it is immune to all attacks and can absorb terrain damage.
